negativeFlows.title: TENNESSEE STATE UNIVERSITY (TSU) IS A MAJOR, COMPREHENSIVE, LAND-GRANT HISTORICALLY BLACK COLLEGE UNIVERSITY (HBCU). TSU IS ACCREDITED BY SACSCOC. ABSTRACT: THE PROGRAM ENDEAVORS TO EMPOWER UNDERREPRESENTED AND MINORITY STUDENTS FOR THRIVING CAREERS IN AVIATION MAINTENANCE. THROUGH COMPREHENSIVE EDUCATIONAL INITIATIVES SUPPORTED BY GRANTS, THE PROGRAM AIMS TO BRIDGE THE GAP BETWEEN THEORETICAL KNOWLEDGE AND PRACTICAL APPLICATION, FOSTERING A SKILLED AND DIVERSE WORKFORCE THAT MEETS INDUSTRY DEMANDS WHILE ENSURING AIRCRAFT SAFETY AND RELIABILITY. WITH A STRONG EMPHASIS ON INCLUSIVITY, THE PROJECT FOCUSES ON INCREASING THE PRESENCE OF UNDERREPRESENTED GROUPS IN THE AVIATION MAINTENANCE WORKFORCE. THE PROJECT PLAN UNFOLDS IN FIVE WELL-DEFINED PHASES, ENCOMPASSING DIVERSE STUDENT AND TEACHER RECRUITMENT, HIGH-QUALITY INSTRUCTION FACILITATED BY EXPERIENCED AVIATION INSTRUCTORS, THE DEVELOPMENT OF PERTINENT AVIATION MAINTENANCE COURSES, ENGAGING AVIATION MAINTENANCE SUMMER CAMPS, AND ACADEMIC AND CAREER COUNSELING TO GUIDE STUDENTS ON THEIR AVIATION JOURNEY. ADDITIONALLY, THE PROGRAM CONDUCTS WORKSHOPS TO RAISE AWARENESS ABOUT THE NUMEROUS OPPORTUNITIES WITHIN THE AVIATION MAINTENANCE INDUSTRY. BY CONTINUOUSLY ASSESSING OUTCOMES THROUGH SURVEYS, INTERVIEWS, AND EVALUATIONS, THE PROGRAM ENSURES ITS EFFECTIVENESS AND CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT. THIS MULTIFACETED APPROACH SUPPORTS OBJECTIVES: IGNITING INTEREST IN AVIATION MAINTENANCE CAREERS, ENHANCING EDUCATION AND TRAINING PROGRAMS TO ALIGN WITH INDUSTRY STANDARDS, AND FOSTERING INDUSTRY PARTNERSHIPS TO PROVIDE STUDENTS WITH INVALUABLE EXPERIENCES AND SEAMLESS TRANSITIONS INTO THE WORKFORCE. THE PROGRAM AIMS TO TRAIN 80 STUDENTS SUCCESSFULLY COMPLETING AVIATION MAINTENANCE COURSES AND OBTAINING RELEVANT CERTIFICATIONS.

THE GOAL OF THE PROPOSED AVIATION WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT (AWD) PROJECT IS TO BUILD THE INTEREST, SKILLS AND KNOWLEDGE NECESSARY FOR HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS TO PURSUE AVIATION-RELATED CAREERS BY ENGAGING THEM IN AUTHENTIC AVIATION EXPERIENCES. ELIZABETH CITY STATE UNIVERSITY (ECSU) WILL SERVE AS THE PRIMARY ENTITY AND PARTNER WITH NORTHEAST ACADEMY FOR AEROSPACE AND ADVANCED TECHNOLOGY (NEAAAT). FURTHER, ECSU WILL LEVERAGE ITS EXISTING PARTNERSHIPS WITH SCHOOL DISTRICTS, NON-PROFIT ORGANIZATIONS, COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS, AND OTHER ENRICHMENT PROGRAMS TO CONDUCT A COMPREHENSIVE OUTREACH PROGRAM FOR HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS IN THE REGION.THE PROPOSED AVIATION WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT (AWD) ACADEMY PROJECT WILL SUPPORT STUDENT DEVELOPMENT THROUGH ACTIVITY COMPONENTS THAT ARE FULLY INTEGRATED TO FORM A COMPREHENSIVE SUPPORT SYSTEM. THE KEY COMPONENTS OF THE PROPOSED AWD PROJECT ARE, (I) AUTHENTIC AVIATION EXPERIENCES, (II) TECHNOLOGY-RICH AVIATION EDUCATION LABORATORY (TR-AEL), AND (III) FAMILY INVOLVEMENT.THE AWD PROGRAM AT ECSU WILL ADOPT THE AIRCRAFT OWNERS AND PILOTS ASSOCIATION (AOPA), THE FAA AVIATION CAREER EDUCATION, AND GRADE APPROPRIATE NASA CURRICULUM AND INTEGRATE VIRTUAL REALITY SIMULATION, UNMANNED AERIAL VEHICLE (UAV) OPERATION, FLIGHT SIMULATOR EXPERIENCE AND DISCOVERY FLIGHT TO ENHANCE AUTHENTIC AND EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING EXPERIENCES. THE PROJECT WILL EXTEND LEARNING TO THE SCHOOL DISTRICTS IN THE FORM OF A MOBILE AEROSPACE EDUCATION LAB, EQUIPPED WITH A STATE-OF-THE-ART DESKTOP FLIGHT SIMULATOR  AIRCRAFT DESIGN STATION, DESKTOP WIND TUNNEL, WEATHER STATION, AND A SET OF HANDS-ON AVIATION-THEMED STEM EXPERIMENTS. THE AWD PROGRAM AT ECSU WILL ALSO FEATURE THE FAMILY CAF, A SPECIAL INTERACTIVE FAMILY INVOLVEMENT FORUM THAT WILL PROVIDE PARENTS AND OTHER ADULT FAMILY MEMBERS WITH INFORMATION, RESOURCES, AND SUPPORT NEEDED TO BECOME AN ACTIVE PARTNER IN THEIR CHILDRENS EDUCATION.DUAL CREDIT COURSES, SUMMER ACADEMY AND YEARLONG SATURDAY ACADEMY, WILL EXPOSE STUDENTS TO STRUCTURED AVIATION TRAINING CURRICULUM AND PREPARE THEM FOR FAA CERTIFICATIONS. THE LEARNING ACTIVITIES HAVE BEEN CAREFULLY DESIGNED TO MEET THE NEXT GENERATION SCIENCE STANDARDS (NGSS) AND THE NORTH CAROLINA STANDARD COURSE OF STUDY FOR SCIENCE AND MATHEMATICS. GUEST SPEAKERS AND FIELD TRIPS WILL COMPLEMENT IN-CLASS LEARNING.THE OBJECTIVE IS TO INCREASE STUDENT INTEREST AND COMPETENCY IN AVIATION-RELATED DISCIPLINES AND SET THEM ON A LEARNING PATH TO BECOME SUCCESSFUL IN COLLEGE AND BEYOND. OVER THE 24-MONTH PROJECT IMPLEMENTATION PERIOD, THE PROPOSED AWD INITIATIVE AT ECSU IS EXPECTED TO DIRECTLY IMPACT 120 HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS, WHERE EACH STUDENT WILL HAVE RECEIVED OVER NINETY (90) HOURS OF LEARNING AND INDIRECTLY IMPACT 1200 STUDENTS THROUGH DAY LONG AND WEEKLONG AVIATION-FOCUSED OUTREACH ACTIVITIES. PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITIES FOR HIGH SCHOOL TEACHERS, COUNSELORS, AND PARENTS WILL ALSO BE AVAILABLE THROUGH ECSUS AWD ACADEMY PROGRAM. FURTHER, THE PROJECT WILL HELP KICK START AVIATION PROGRAM IN TWO HIGH SCHOOLS LOCATED IN UNDERSERVED COUNTIES.THE PROJECT TEAM IS COMMITTED TO CONDUCTING BOTH FORMATIVE AND SUMMATIVE EVALUATION AND REPORT RESULTS TO THE FAA ON A REGULAR BASIS. ADDITIONALLY, THE PROJECT TEAM WILL DISSEMINATE PROJECT RESULTS THROUGH A DEDICATED WEBSITE, SOCIAL MEDIA, PROGRAM BROCHURES, NEWS RELEASES, PROJECT NEWSLETTERS, AND PUBLICATIONS IN TECHNICAL AND EDUCATIONAL CONFERENCES JOURNALS.

MCTCS ELIGIBILITY AS AN ENTITY TO APPLY FOR THIS GRANT IS BASED ON ITS STATUS AS AN ACCREDITED INSTITUTION OF HIGHER EDUCATION. THE MCTC AVIATION WORKFORCE EMPOWERMENT PROGRAM (AWEP) PROPOSAL FALLS UNDER THE ELIGIBLE PROJECT TYPES:A. PROJECTS THAT ESTABLISH NEW EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMS THAT TEACH TECHNICAL SKILLS USED IN AVIATION MAINTENANCE  C. PROJECTS THAT SUPPORT OUTREACH ABOUT CAREERS IN THE AVIATION MAINTENANCE INDUSTRY TO SECONDARY SCHOOL STUDENTS AND COMMUNITIES UNDERREPRESENTED IN THE INDUSTRY  D. PROJECTS THAT SUPPORT EDUCATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES RELATED TO AVIATION MAINTENANCE IN ECONOMICALLY DISADVANTAGED GEOGRAPHIC AREAS  E. PROJECTS THAT SUPPORT THE TRANSITION TO CAREERS IN AVIATION MAINTENANCE.THE AVIATION INDUSTRY FACES A CRITICAL CHALLENGE: A GROWING SHORTAGE OF SKILLED AVIATION MAINTENANCE TECHNICIANS (AMTS). DESPITE THE INDUSTRY S PROJECTED 4.1% GROWTH RATE TILL 2032 AND 3% GLOBAL CARGO FLEET EXPANSION, THE SHORTAGE OF AMTS PERSISTS, POSING OPERATIONAL AND SAFETY RISKS. KENTUCKY S THRIVING AVIATION AND AEROSPACE SECTOR PROJECTS A 15% SURGE IN AMT DEMAND BY 2030, REQUIRING 270 ANNUAL OPENINGS AND TOTALING 3,020 POSITIONS. THIS SCARCITY ENDANGERS AIRCRAFT SAFETY, EXTENDS DOWNTIMES, AND HAMPERS EFFICIENCY. THE MCTC AVIATION WORKFORCE EMPOWERMENT PROGRAM (AWEP) PROJECT TACKLES THE SCARCITY OF SKILLED AVIATION MAINTENANCE TECHNICIANS AND REGIONAL INEQUALITIES BY PROVIDING AN EXTENDED FAA-CERTIFIED CURRICULUM, INTERACTIVE AND ENGAGING CAREER WORKSHOPS FOR MIDDLE SCHOOL STUDENTS, AND TARGETED EQUITY-FOCUSED SESSIONS FOR HIGH SCHOOLERS TO PRODUCE HIGHLY PREPARED AMTS COLLABORATING WITH EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS, INDUSTRY EXPERTS, EXPERIMENTAL AIRCRAFT ASSOCIATION (EAA) CHAPTERS, AND LOCAL SCHOOL DISTRICTS, AWEP AIMS TO EMPOWER STUDENTS AND CULTIVATE A HIGHLY PREPARED AMT WORKFORCE, BOLSTERING THE AVIATION SECTOR.THE AWEP PROJECT LEVERAGES OPPORTUNITIES GAINED FROM PAST INVESTMENTS FROM THE FEDERAL AVIATION ADMINISTRATION AND THE KENTUCKY DEPARTMENT OF AVIATION THAT LEAD TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF A NEW RUNWAY, AIRPORT PARKING, LIGHTING, AND HANGARS AT THE FLEMING-MASON AIRPORT LOCATED WITHIN MINUTES OF MCTCS MAYSVILLE CAMPUS.

PACIFIC AVIATION NORTHWEST OFFERS FLIGHT INSTRUCTION UNDER PART 61 OF TITLE 14, CODE OF FEDERAL REGULATIONS WITH THE ASSISTANCE OF OUR EXPERIENCED STAFF OF CERTIFIED FLIGHT INSTRUCTORS (CFI) AND CERTIFIED INSTRUMENT INSTRUCTORS (CFII), WHO ADHERE TO ALL FAA GUIDELINES AND PROTOCOLS. OUR DEDICATION IS TO IMPROVE OUR EXISTING CURRICULUM FOR HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS, EQUIPPING THEM WITH SKILLS CRUCIAL FOR ENTERING THE INDUSTRY AS A PILOT. WE ARE ESTABLISHING A COMPREHENSIVE CURRICULUM FOR TRAINING UNMANNED AIRCRAFT SYSTEMS OPERATORS. BY BROADENING OUR TRAINING PROGRAMS TO INCLUDE THESE COURSES, WITH A FOCUS ON FACE-TO-FACE EDUCATION, WERE MAKING THEM MORE ACCESSIBLE TO THOSE WHO ARE UNDERSERVED IN THE COMMUNITY.  OUR STRATEGY IS GEARED TOWARDS EMPOWERING STUDENTS WITH THE SKILLS ESSENTIAL FOR A CAREER AS AN AIRCRAFT OR REMOTE PILOT. THE PROJECT WILL BROADEN THE REACH OF HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS IN RESPONSE TO THE ESCALATING DEMAND FOR AIRCRAFT AND REMOTE PILOTS AND INCREASE THE IN-CLASS TRAINING OPTIONS FOR REMOTE PILOT TRAINING THAT IS LIMITED IN THE AREA. OUR PRIMARY PURPOSE IS TO FOSTER A PASSION FOR AVIATION AMONG STUDENTS AND PROVIDE THEM WITH A COMPREHENSIVE UNDERSTANDING OF THE POTENTIAL CAREER PATHS THAT CAN BE ATTAINED THROUGH OUR TRAINING PROGRAMS. THE PROJECT WILL ENABLE STUDENTS FROM JOSEPHINE AND JACKSON COUNTIES, ESPECIALLY THOSE FROM UNDERREPRESENTED RURAL AREAS TO ACCESS TRAINING RESOURCES AND EXPAND THEIR EDUCATIONAL CAREER OPPORTUNITIES. AS THE PROJECT EVOLVES, WE AIM TO EXTEND ITS REACH TO NEIGHBORING COUNTIES IN YEARS TO COME. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES WILL INCLUDE (1) INCREASED STUDENT OUTREACH PROGRAMS IN BOTH JOSEPHINE AND JACKSON COUNTIES. THIS WILL INCREASE STUDENT ENROLLMENT FOR FLIGHT INSTRUCTION WITH THE FINAL GOAL OF THEM OBTAINING THEIR PILOT LICENSE. (2) CREATE AND EXECUTE A TRAINING PROGRAM FOR UNMANNED AIRCRAFT SYSTEMS OPERATORS THAT AIMS TO ENABLE STUDENTS TO ACQUIRE THEIR REMOTE PILOT CERTIFICATE. IT IS ALSO NECESSARY TO PROVIDE TRAIN-THE-TRAINER INSTRUCTION FOR AT LEAST ONE OF OUR EXISTING FLIGHT INSTRUCTORS. (3) RECRUIT AN OUTREACH CAREER COUNSELING COORDINATOR AND A SOCIAL MEDIA MARKETING COORDINATOR TO GENERATE ENTHUSIASM AND INCREASE AWARENESS ABOUT VARIOUS CAREER PATH OPTIONS.  HIRING THEM WILL BROADEN OUR OUTREACH ACTIVITIES IN AREAS THAT HAVE BEEN UNDERREPRESENTED, CREATING ACCESS AND OPPORTUNITIES THAT MAY OTHERWISE GO UNNOTICED. (4) ESTABLISHING A MODERNIZED LEARNING ATMOSPHERE, IN BOTH LEARNING LOCATIONS, BY INTEGRATING CUTTING-EDGE RESOURCES LIKE SOPHISTICATED TECHNOLOGY, INSTRUCTIONAL TOOLS, AND COMFORTABLE PHYSICAL FACILITIES WILL FOSTER A PRODUCTIVE EDUCATIONAL ENVIRONMENT. STUDENTS WILL BENEFIT FROM STATE-OF-THE-ART TECHNOLOGY, ELECTRONIC DEVICES, UPDATED FURNITURE, EQUIPMENT UPGRADES, AND FLIGHT SIMULATION SYSTEMS. THE PROJECT OBJECTIVE WILL BE ACCOMPLISHED BY (1) STAFF WILL BE EQUIPPED WITH PROMOTIONAL INFORMATIONAL MATERIALS, AND VISUAL AIDS TO PROMOTE AT HIGH SCHOOLS, CAREER FAIRS, FLY-IN AND CAREER DAYS IN THE SURROUNDING AREAS TO ENGAGE EDUCATE STUDENTS ON OPTIONS AVAILABLE. THE TIMEFRAME WILL BE THE FULL DURATION OF THE PROGRAM AND WILL INVOLVE PROCUREMENT AND INVOLVEMENT. (2) CURRICULUM OPTIONS ARE PRESENTLY BEING EVALUATED IN OUR ORGANIZATION. FOR SEVERAL YEARS, THE AVIATION INDUSTRY HAS PREDICTED A SHORTAGE OF PILOTS AND MECHANICS. THAT SHORTAGE HAS NOW REACHED CRITICAL LEVELS. IT IS REQUIRED BY THE FAA, THAT AIRCRAFT MECHANICS HAVE 1900 HOURS OF CLASSROOM AND HANDS ON TRAINING. THIS MEANS A STUDENT WILL NEED A 2 YEAR EDUCATION BEFORE ENTERING THE WORKFORCE. ONCE THE AIRFRAME AND POWERPLANT (A P) LICENSING IS COMPLETE, THEN THEY CAN START BUILDING EXPERIENCE IN THE FIELD.  ADVANCED HELICOPTER SERVICES PROPOSES TO LAUNCH AN APPRENTICE PROGRAM TO ALLOW CANDIDATES THE OPPORTUNITY TO EARN A LIVING AND GAIN VALUABLE EXPERIENCE WHILE GETTING THE EDUCATION THEY NEED TO OBTAIN THEIR AIRFRAME AND POWERPLANT LICENSE . OUR AIM IS TO PRODUCE WELL QUALIFIED MECHANICS WITH HELICOPTER EXPERIENCE IN THE TIME IT WOULD TAKE SOMEONE TO GRADUATE FROM A CERTIFIED SCHOOL. WE CAN ALSO ADAPT THE TRAINING FOR SOMEONE WHO HAS SOME EXPERIENCE OUT OF THE MILITARY ALLOWING THEM TO JOIN THE WORK FORCE MUCH SOONER. IT IS OUR GOAL TO GRADUATE 10 STUDENTS PER YEAR OUT OF THIS PROGRAM AT A MINIMUM.

IOWA WESTERN COMMUNITY COLLEGE (IWCC), AN ACCREDITED TWO-YEAR PUBLIC COLLEGE LOCATED IN COUNCIL BLUFFS, IA, IS PROPOSING A 24-MONTH PROJECT TO EXPAND THE AVIATION MAINTENANCE TECHNICIAN WORKFORCE IN SOUTHWEST IOWA AND NEIGHBORING EASTERN NEBRASKA BY IMPROVING THE COLLEGES FAA-CERTIFIED AIRCRAFT MAINTENANCE TECHNICIAN SCHOOL (AMTS). THE PROPOSAL ADDRESSES PROJECT AREAS A, B, C, D, E, AND F AS ESTABLISHED IN SECTION 625(D) OF THE FAA REAUTHORIZATION ACT OF 2023 (PUB. L. NO. 115-254).PROJECT DREAM (DRIVE RETENTION AND EXPAND AVIATION MAINTENANCE) WILL AMPLIFY THE REGIONS AVIATION MAINTENANCE TECHNICIAN WORKFORCE BY 1) SUSTAINING AND ADVANCING OUTREACH AND RECRUITMENT CAMPAIGNS DESIGNED TO ATTRACT A DIVERSE POOL OF CANDIDATES  2) EXPANDING PROGRAM CAPACITY  3) ENHANCING STUDENT SUPPORT SERVICES  AND 4) IMPROVING THE EDUCATIONAL EXPERIENCE THROUGH UPDATES TO INSTRUCTIONAL EQUIPMENT AND TECHNOLOGY. THESE DEFINED GOALS WILL INCREASE AWARENESS OF CAREERS IN AVIATION MAINTENANCE TECHNOLOGY (AMT) AMONG PROSPECTIVE STUDENTS AND LOCAL COMMUNITIES. FURTHER, THEY WILL EASE THE TRANSITION TO CAREERS IN AVIATION MAINTENANCE FOR VETERANS, HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS, AND ADULT JOB SEEKERS FROM SPECIAL POPULATIONS HISTORICALLY UNDERSERVED AND UNDERREPRESENTED WITHIN THE INDUSTRY, AS WELL AS THOSE RESIDING IN ECONOMICALLY DISADVANTAGED REGIONS. FINALLY, THEY WILL DELIVER FINANCIAL AND ACADEMIC ASSISTANCE TO CURRENT AMT STUDENTS, AND ENSURE PROGRAM GRADUATES ARE PREPARED WITH THE SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE, AND COMPETENCIES NEEDED TO SUCCESSFULLY PARTICIPATE IN THE MODERN WORKFORCE.IWCC IS THE SOLE APPLICANT FOR THIS PROPOSAL. THE COLLEGE WILL MAGNIFY EXISTING RECRUITMENT EFFORTS BY CONTINUING TO LEVERAGE THE RESOURCES OF ITS ON-CAMPUS VETERANS CENTER AND AREA VETERAN ORGANIZATIONS. THE COLLEGE WILL MAINTAIN ITS STRONG PARTNERSHIPS WITH THE COUNCIL BLUFFS COMMUNITY SCHOOL DISTRICT (CBCSD) IN COUNCIL BLUFFS, IOWA, AND OMAHA PUBLIC SCHOOLS (OPS) IN OMAHA, NEBRASKA. THIS IS IN ADDITION TO ONGOING PARTNERSHIPS WITH IOWAWORKS IN COUNCIL BLUFFS, IOWA, AND HEARTLAND WORKFORCE SOLUTIONS IN OMAHA, NEBRASKATWO PIVOTAL ORGANIZATIONS THAT SERVE AS THE REGIONS WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT ENTITIES AND AMERICAN JOBS CENTERS.FURTHERMORE, PROJECT DREAM WILL FOCUS ON THE RETENTION OF THE PROGRAMS CURRENT STUDENTS. THE INITIATIVE WILL UTILIZE STUDENT SCHOLARSHIPS TO BRIDGE THE BUDGETARY GAP BETWEEN PROGRAM-RELATED FEES AND TRADITIONAL FINANCIAL AID. REFINEMENT OF EXISTING TUTORING, PEER MENTORING, AND AMBASSADOR PROGRAMS WILL SUPPLEMENT CURRENT COLLEGE-WIDE STUDENT SUPPORT SERVICES. FINALLY, THE MODERNIZATION OF EXISTING INSTRUCTIONAL TECHNOLOGIES AND EQUIPMENT WILL SERVE AS AN INTEGRAL PART OF MEETING RETAINMENT GOALS. BY REPLACING ANTIQUATED CLASSROOM EQUIPMENT AND SUPPLIES, AMT PROGRAM STAFF WILL PROVIDE STUDENTS WITH THE MOST RELEVANT AND UP-TO-DATE TRAINING AVAILABLE. THE ACTIVITIES PROPOSED IN THIS ABSTRACT ARE A CONTINUATION OF AN EXISTING PROJECT.

AAR IS THE LARGEST MAINTENANCE REPAIR AND OVERHAUL FACILITY IN NORTH AMERICA. AAR EMPLOYS OVER 3,500 AVIATION MAINTENANCE TECHNICIANS IN ITS FOUR MRO FACILITIES EACH REGULATED BY CFR PART 145 MAKING AAR ELIGIBLE FOR THIS GRANT.  OUR PROJECT FITS INTO THREE CATEGORIES: APPRENTICESHIP, OUTREACH TO CAREERS IN AVIATION MAINTENANCE AND SUPPORT OF TRANSITIONING MILITARY PERSONNEL.  IN 2018, AAR LAUNCHED THE EAGLE CAREER PATHWAY PROGRAM THAT IS USED BY OUR PARTNER COLLEGES AND UNIVERSITIES TO MARKET AND GROW THE AVIATION MAINTENANCE TECHNICIAN PIPELINE.  EAGLE PARTNERS SCHOOLS ARE JUST ONE COMPONENT OF AARS WORKFORCE STRATEGY THAT IS ALSO FOCUSED ON SHORT CREDENTIALING PROGRAMS, TRANSITIONING MILITARY PERSONNEL AND CHANGING THE DEMOGRAPHICS OF OUR INDUSTRY WITH A FOCUSED ON THE UNDERREPRESENTED IN AVIATION SPECIFICALLY WOMEN AND PEOPLE OF COLOR.   AAR WILL FOCUS ALL $500,000 IN EXPANDING OUR APPRENTICESHIP PROGRAM THAT CURRENTLY IS APPROVED BY THE US DEPARTMENT OF LABOR AND US DEPARTMENT OF VETERAN AFFAIRS BEYOND OUR FOUR MRO FACILITIES TO INCLUDE OUR LANDING GEAR AND COMPONENT REPAIR FACILITIES LOCATED IN MIAMI, FLORIDA AND GARDEN CITY, NEW YORK RESPECTIVELY. IN ADDITION TO EXPANDING LOCATIONS AAR WILL GROW THE NUMBER OF APPRENTICES BY 100 THROUGH A COMBINATION OF COHORT HIRING OF FEMALE TECHNICIANS, EXPANDING THE NUMBER OF TRANSITIONING MILITARY PERSONNEL CHOOSING AVIATION TECHNICAL CAREERS THROUGH OUR SKILLBRIDGE PROGRAM AND EXPANDING THE NUMBER OF HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS ENROLLED IN OUR APPRENTICESHIP PROGRAM.  AAR IS ABSORBING ALL ADMINISTRATIVE COSTS OF THIS GRANT TO ENSURE THAT ALL THE FUNDING IS DIRECTED TO GROWING THE TECHNICIAN WORKFORCE AND WE BELIEVE THAT THIS PROPOSAL WILL DO JUST THAT.

ELIGIBLE APPLICANT CATEGORY (A): AS THE HOLDER OF A PART 135 AIR OPERATOR CERTIFICATE, JOBY ELEVATE IS ELIGIBLE FOR THE PROGRAM.ELIGIBLE PROJECT CATEGORIES: THIS PROJECT IS ELIGIBLE FOR AWARD UNDER CATEGORIES A, B, C, D, E, AND F (ALL CATEGORIES).PROJECT OVERVIEW: THIS PROJECT WILL PROVIDE A NEW, MORE ACCESSIBLE AVIATION MAINTENANCE TECHNICIAN (AMT) CAREER PATH, ENABLING TRAINEES TO BEGIN A PAID MECHANIC APPRENTICESHIP IMMEDIATELY AFTER COMPLETING THE LIGHT SPORT REPAIRMAN - MAINTENANCE (LSRM) CERTIFICATION PROGRAM. THIS PATHWAY ALLOWS FOR THE ASPIRING AVIATION MECHANIC TO EARN A WAGE WHILE THEY ARE IN TRAINING. AFTER COMPLETING THE PAID 30 MONTH APPRENTICESHIP, TRAINEES WILL QUALIFY TO ATTAIN THEIR A P AND GAIN FURTHER EMPLOYMENT AS A CERTIFICATED AMT. THIS CAREER PATHWAY DEVELOPED BY JOBY ELEVATE CONSISTS OF FIVE PHASES SPANNING 30 MONTHS: 1) COMPLETE THE LSRM CERTIFICATION PROGRAM  2) COMPLETE A 12 MONTH LSA APPRENTICESHIP ROTATION  3) COMPLETE AN 18 MONTH AAM APPRENTICESHIP ROTATION  4) SUBMIT THE DOCUMENTED EVIDENCE PACKAGE  5) COMPLETE CERTIFICATION EXAMS AND BECOME A CERTIFICATED A P.OBJECTIVES: THIS PROJECT SEEKS TO: 1) INSPIRE YOUTH AND ADULTS TO PURSUE A CAREER IN AVIATION MAINTENANCE  2) MAKE THE LIGHT SPORT REPAIRMAN - MAINTENANCE (LSRM) CERTIFICATION MORE ACCESSIBLE TO THE PUBLIC AND CREATE A NEW ENTRY POINT TO THE AMT CAREER  3) PROVIDE A SCALABLE, WIDELY ACCESSIBLE CAREER PATH THROUGH PAID APPRENTICESHIPS  4) MAKE AMT CAREERS AVAILABLE TO MORE WOMEN, PEOPLE OF COLOR, VETERANS, AND UNDERSERVED POPULATIONS.IN PARTNERSHIP WITH JOBY AVIATION COLLEGE, A DELAWARE PUBLIC BENEFIT CORPORATION AND PART 61 PILOT SCHOOL (AND PART 141 APPLICANT), AND JOBY AERO, AN EVTOL (ELECTRIC VERTICAL TAKEOFF AND LANDING) MANUFACTURER, JOBY ELEVATE WILL DEVELOP THE CURRICULA AND PROGRAMS NECESSARY TO ACCOMPLISH THE PROJECT OBJECTIVES. ESTABLISHING AND DELIVERING THESE TRAINING AND APPRENTICESHIP PROGRAMS WILL CREATE NEW AMT CAREER OPPORTUNITIES FOR INDIVIDUALS ACROSS THE US.

THOMAS UNIVERSITY AVIATION MAINTENANCE TECHNICIAN (AMT) PROGRAM.FUNDING OPPORTUNITY NUMBER: 23-FAA-AWD-AMELIGIBILITY STATEMENTS:THOMAS UNIVERSITY IS AN ACCREDITED INSTITUTION OF HIGHER EDUCATION (AS DEFINED IN SECTION 101 OF THE HIGHER EDUCATION ACT OF 1965 (20 U.S.C.  1001)) THOMAS UNIVERSITYS PROPOSED PROJECT ESTABLISHES A NEW EDUCATIONAL PROGRAM THAT TEACHES TECHNICAL SKILLS USED IN AVIATION MAINTENANCE AS WELL AS PURCHASING EQUIPMENT FOR THE PROPOSED PROGRAM.ABSTRACT: THOMAS UNIVERSITY WILL DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT A NEW AVIATION MAINTENANCE TECHNICIAN (AMT) TRAINING PROGRAM ENHANCING EDUCATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES FOR A DIVERSE GROUP OF STUDENTS INCLUDING THOSE FROM UNDERREPRESENTED COMMUNITIES, ECONOMICALLY DISADVANTAGED AREAS, WOMEN, PEOPLE OF COLOR, AND TRAINING FOR SEPARATED VETERANS. THIS PROGRAM WILL CREATE A SUSTAINABLE PIPELINE OF AVIATION MAINTENANCE TECHNICIANS (AMTS) TO FILL THE NEED OF THE AVIATION MAINTENANCE INDUSTRY AND PROVIDE GRADUATES WITH HIGH PAYING JOBS.THOMAS UNIVERSITYS AVIATION MAINTENANCE TECHNICIAN (AMT) PROGRAM WILL FILL THE WORKFORCE GAP IN THE AVIATION MAINTENANCE INDUSTRY BY TRAINING STUDENTS IN THE UNDERSERVED AREA. THROUGH A CONCRETE WORK PLAN AND GRANT FUNDING, THOMAS UNIVERSITY WILL EXECUTE THE PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT, ACQUIRE EQUIPMENT, SET UP FACILITIES, AND BE AWARDED FEDERAL AVIATION ADMINISTRATION (FAA) PART 147 CERTIFICATION PAVING THE WAY FOR STUDENTS FROM ALL BACKGROUNDS TO FILL THE WORKFORCE SHORTAGES. THOMAS UNIVERSITYS PROPOSED PROJECT WILL PROVIDE THE CAPACITY FOR FIFTY NEW STUDENTS PER YEAR TO BE TRAINED. PROPOSED FIRST CLASS START DATE IN THE FALL OF 2024.

THE AERONAUTICS PROGRAM AT SAN BERNARDINO VALLEY COLLEGE (SBVC), WHICH IS FULLY ACCREDITED BY THE ACCREDITING COMMISSION FOR COMMUNITY AND JUNIOR COLLEGES (ACCJC), HAS A LONGSTANDING AND WELL-RESPECTED HISTORY IN THE FIELD OF AVIATION.  PER THE AUTHORIZING LEGISLATION, THE PROPOSED PROJECT WOULD ENABLE SBVC TO EXPAND OUR AVIATION MECHANICS AIRFRAME AND POWERPLANT TECHNOLOGY PROGRAM TO HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS  IMPROVE OUR EXISTING PROGRAM WITH UP-TO-DATE TECHNOLOGIES  ESTABLISH SCHOLARSHIPS FOR STUDENTS PURSUING EMPLOYMENT IN THE AVIATION MAINTENANCE INDUSTRY  SUPPORT LOCAL COMMUNITY OUTREACH ABOUT CAREERS IN AVIATION  AND SUPPORT EDUCATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES RELATED TO AVIATION MAINTENANCE IN AN ECONOMICALLY DISADVANTAGED REGION.SITUATED AT THE CONVERGENCE OF THREE CITIESSAN BERNARDINO, COLTON, AND RIALTOSBVC SERVES A COMPLEX AND DIVERSE STUDENT POPULATION, MANY OF WHOM HAIL FROM ONE OF THE THIRTY-THREE (33) QUALIFIED ZONES OF OPPORTUNITY LOCATED IN THE COLLEGES IMMEDIATE SERVICE AREA.  THE MAJORITY OF OUR STUDENT BODY ARE REFLECTIVE OF THE SURROUNDING COMMUNITIESPRIMARILY LATINX (67.3%), FIRST-GENERATION COLLEGE STUDENTS (73%), AND LOW-INCOME (65.3%).  THESE DEMOGRAPHICS ARE ALSO REPRESENTATIVE OF MANY OF THE HIGH SCHOOLS AND K-12 DISTRICTS SBVC SERVES AND WITH WHOM THE COLLEGE HAS EXISTING DUAL ENROLLMENT AGREEMENTS.THE PROPOSED PROJECT WOULD ALLOW SAN BERNARDINO VALLEY COLLEGE TO LEVERAGE ITS EXISTING RELATIONSHIPS WITH LOCAL HIGH SCHOOLS AND K-12 DISTRICTS TO EXPAND OUR SUCCESSFUL AVIATION MECHANICS AIRFRAME AND POWERPLANT TECHNOLOGY PROGRAM TO SERVE AN INCREASED NUMBER OF STUDENTS.  AT THE CENTER OF OUR PROPOSED PROJECT IS THE CORE GOAL OF SUCCESSFULLY PREPARING STUDENTS TO SERVE THE ANTICIPATED DEMANDS OF THE U.S. AVIATION INDUSTRY BY PROVIDING THE EDUCATION NECESSARY TO GAIN THE SKILLS AND TRAINING NECESSARY TO SECURE ABOVE-LIVING WAGE CAREER TRAJECTORIES, POTENTIALLY TRANSFORMING THE SOCIOECONOMIC STATUS AND LIFE TRAJECTORIES OF GENERATIONS OF MARGINALIZED PEOPLE IN THE AREA.  PRIMARY GOALS OF THE PROJECT WILL FOCUS ON: 1) RECRUITMENT  2) REGISTRATION AND RETENTION  3) PROGRAM COMPLETION  AND 4) CERTIFICATION.AS A COMMITMENT TO AND IN SUPPORT OF THE PROPOSED PROJECT, SBVC WILL PROVIDE, AT MINIMUM, $106,000 VIA IN-KIND CONTRIBUTIONS, INCLUDING PERSONNEL COSTS AND BENEFITS, MARKETING AND RECRUITING COSTS, AND TRAVEL WHERE APPLICABLE.  IN ORDER TO BRING THE PROJECT TO FULL FRUITION, SVBC IS REQUESTING $498,555 IN FEDERAL FUNDS FOR YEAR 1.  THESE FUNDS WILL BE USED PRIMARILY TO: 1) UPGRADE CURRENT EQUIPMENT TO INCLUDE MORE UP-TO-DATE AND STATE-OF-THE-ART TECHNOLOGIES  2) PURCHASE NECESSARY SUPPLIES FOR THE AFOREMENTIONED EQUIPMENT AND PARTICIPANTS  AND 3) ESTABLISH AND AWARD SCHOLARSHIPS FOR STUDENTS TO DEFRAY THE COSTS OF FAA CERTIFICATION EXAMS AND TO COVER DEFER THE COSTS OF THE TOOL BOXES STUDENTS NEED IN ORDER TO BEGIN WORK.BY CAPITALIZING ON SBVCS ESTABLISHED AVIATION MECHANICS AIRFRAME AND POWERPLANT TECHNOLOGY PROGRAM AND LEVERAGING EXISTING POSITIVE RELATIONSHIPS WITH LOCAL K-12 DISTRICTS, THE PROPOSED PROJECT AIMS TO NOT ONLY INCREASE THE POOL OF FAA-CERTIFIED AIRCRAFT MAINTENANCE TECHNICAL WORKERS WITHIN THE REGION, BUT ALSO TO PREPARE STUDENTS FOR POTENTIALLY LIFE-CHANGING OPPORTUNITIES AND CAREERS IN THE FIELD OF AVIATION.  STUDENT SUCCESS THROUGH THE PROPOSED PROJECT MAY VERY WELL LEAD TO ENTIRE FAMILIES WITHIN OUR COMMUNITY AND REGION BEING LIFTED OUT OF THE CYCLE OF POVERTY.

THE AVIATION AND AEROSPACE INDUSTRY IS PREDICTED TO GROW RAPIDLY OVER THE NEXT TWO DECADES, WITH THE RECENT REPORTS FROM THE AVIATION TECHNICIAN EDUCATION COUNCIL (ATEC) AND BOEING SUGGESTING THE INDUSTRY WILL NEED 690,000 NEW TECHNICIANS OVER THE NEXT 20 YEARS NECESSITATING A 20% GROWTH IN AVIATION PERSONNEL. WITH THE CHALLENGE LYING IN PROGRAM AWARENESS INDICATED BY THE PIPELINE GROWING AT ONLY ABOUT 2%, THE WE AIM PROJECT TEAM PROPOSES TO BUILD ON A SUCCESSFUL PILOT TEST OF AVIATION MAINTENANCE ONLINE CURRICULUM CONDUCTED IN 2022-23 ACROSS 9 SCHOOLS IN THE US. WE AIMS MISSION IS TO REFINE AND CURATE THE NEXT GENERATION AVIATION MAINTENANCE CURRICULUM, DEPLOY TO HIGH SCHOOLS AND TECHNICAL COLLEGES NATIONALLY, AND BUILD PATHWAYS TO EMPLOYMENT AND OR OPPORTUNITIES TO INCLUDE MECHANIC CERTIFICATIONS. WE AIM IS A PARTNERSHIP BETWEEN THE LEAD ENTITY, CLEMSON UNIVERSITY S CENTER FOR WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT (CUCWD), CHOOSE AEROSPACE, THE AVIATION TECHNICIAN EDUCATION COUNCIL (ATEC), THE NSF ADVANCED TECHNOLOGICAL EDUCATION (ATE) CENTER FOR AVIATION AND AUTOMOTIVE TECHNICIAN EDUCATION USING VIRTUAL E-SCHOOLS (CA2VES), AND GREENVILLE TECHNICAL COLLEGE (GTC). TOGETHER, AND IN COORDINATION WITH A COALITION OF AEROSPACE STAKEHOLDERS, THE TEAM DEVELOPED THE CHOOSE AEROSPACE AVIATION MAINTENANCE CURRICULUM, A COMPUTER-BASED PROGRAM SPECIFICALLY DESIGNED TO INCREASE THE NUMBER OF INDIVIDUALS EXPOSED TO CAREERS IN AVIATION MAINTENANCE AND BUILD WORKFORCE PIPELINES DIRECTLY INTO AVIATION CAREERS. IN A 2022 PILOT PROJECT, 140 STUDENTS ENGAGED WITH A DEMOGRAPHIC OF MORE THAN 60% NON-WHITE AND 12% FEMALE. THIS PROPOSAL EXPANDS THE PROJECT TO 500 STUDENTS DURING THE PROJECT YEAR, WITH AN ADDITIONAL 1000 STUDENTS OVER THE FOLLOWING TWO YEARS. WE AIM WILL SPECIFICALLY EMPHASIZE DEPLOYMENT IN OPPORTUNITY ZONES AND HIGH SCHOOLS WITH TRIO PROGRAMS. THROUGH COLLABORATION WITH COMMUNITY AND STUDENT ORGANIZATIONS, THE TEAM WILL IDENTIFY BEST PRACTICES FOR TARGETING WOMEN, RURAL STUDENTS, AND OTHER UNDERSERVED POPULATIONS.WE AIM WILL 1) FACILITATE CONTINUAL IMPROVEMENT TO THE CONTENT SPECIFICALLY FOCUSED ON REFINING AND ENHANCING HANDS-ON ACTIVITIES AND TEACHER GUIDES AND RESOURCES, 2) BUILD REPORTING AND ANALYSIS FEATURES INTO THE CURRICULUM PLATFORM TO ENSURE OUTCOMES ARE ACHIEVED AND TO CONTINUALLY ASSESS STUDENT PERFORMANCE IN ORDER TO IMPROVE TRAINING, 3) REMOVE BARRIERS TO ADOPTION, 4) DEVELOP AND CLEARLY COMMUNICATE PATHWAYS AVAILABLE TO STUDENTS, 5) SCALE AND EXPAND THE PROGRAM TO AN ADDITIONAL 1,000 STUDENTS CROSS THE UNITED STATES THROUGH OUTREACH AND MARKETING, WITH A SPECIFIC EMPHASIS ON REACHING UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES, AND 6) DEVELOP A PLAN TO ENSURE LONG-TERM SUSTAINABILITY OF THE PROGRAM. WE AIM PROPOSES THE FOLLOWING GOALS: GOAL 1. FACILITATE CONTINUAL IMPROVEMENT TO THE CONTENT SPECIFICALLY FOCUSED ON REFINING AND ENHANCING HANDS-ON ACTIVITIES AND TEACHER GUIDES AND RESOURCES. GOAL 2. EDUCATE COMMUNITIES AND CREATE WIDE-SPREAD ADOPTION OF THE GENERAL CURRICULUM IN HIGH SCHOOLS, CREATE OPPORTUNITIES FOR SECONDARY STUDENTS TO TRANSFER CREDITS EARNED TO ANY FAA-CERTIFICATED AVIATION MAINTENANCE TECHNICIAN SCHOOL, AND CONTINUALLY ASSESS THE PROGRAM TO ENSURE LEARNING OUTCOMES ARE ACHIEVED. GOAL 3. DEPLOY CURRICULUM IN UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES, INCREASE AWARENESS, AND RECRUIT DIVERSE STUDENTS INTO AVIATION MAINTENANCE CAREERS. GOAL 4. DEVELOP A LONG-TERM SUSTAINABILITY PLAN TO SCALE THE CURRICULUM TO HIGH SCHOOLS AND DUAL CREDIT PROGRAMS NATIONALLY. WE AIM ADDRESSES PREDICTED AVIATION INDUSTRY GROWTH AND SHORTAGES THROUGH TRAINING BEGINNING IN HIGH SCHOOL. THE CURRICULUM ALIGNS WITH THE NEW FAA MECHANIC AIRMAN CERTIFICATION STANDARDS AND IS A DIRECT PATH TO FAA MECHANIC CERTIFICATION. THE DELIBERATE PROJECT DESIGN IS FOCUSED ON AWARENESS AND RECRUITMENT OF THOSE UNDERREPRESENTED IN THE AMT WORKFORCE.WE AIM MEETS THE ELIGIBILITY REQUIREMENT ELIGIBLE APPLICANTS - CATEGORIES A, B, AND C   ELIGIBLE PROJECTS -  CATEGORIES A, B, C, D, AND F.

LEWIS UNIVERSITY S PROJECT S.O.A.R. (SUPPORTING OPPORTUNITIES IN AVIATION RESILIENCE) WILL INCREASE THE NUMBER, DIVERSITY, AND CAREER READINESS OF AVIATION MAINTENANCE PROFESSIONALS FROM UNDERREPRESENTED BACKGROUNDS, INCLUDING WOMEN, HISPANIC AND AFRICAN AMERICAN BLACK STUDENTS, FIRST-GENERATION, AND LOW-INCOME PELL-ELIGIBLE STUDENTS IN THE CHICAGOLAND AREA. LEWIS UNIVERSITY (LU) IS AN ELIGIBLE APPLICANT IN THE CATEGORY OF INSTITUTION OF HIGHER EDUCATION. THE UNIVERSITY IS ACCREDITED BY THE HIGHER LEARNING COMMISSION. LEWISS AVIATION MAINTENANCE TECHNICIAN SCHOOL AND OTHER AVIATION PROGRAMS ARE APPROVED BY THE FAA UNDER TITLE 14 OF THE CODE OF FEDERAL REGULATIONS (CFR). LUS PROJECT SOAR IS AN ELIGIBLE PROJECT, BELONGING TO MULTIPLE PROJECT CATEGORIES: (B) ESTABLISHING SCHOLARSHIPS  (C) SUPPORTING OUTREACH TO SECONDARY SCHOOL STUDENTS, (D) SUPPORTING OPPORTUNITIES IN ECONOMICALLY DISADVANTAGED GEOGRAPHIC AREAS, AND (F) ENHANCING AVIATION MAINTENANCE TECHNICAL EDUCATION. PROJECT SOAR LEVERAGES KEY EDUCATIONAL PARTNERS IN DIVERSE COMMUNITIES: ST. AUGUSTINE COLLEGE (SAC), A HISPANIC-SERVING INSTITUTION (HSI), AND DUAL CREDIT PARTNERS TOWNSHIP HIGH SCHOOL DISTRICT 214 AND WILL COUNTY AREA CAREER CENTER (WILCO). ADDITIONALLY, THE CPASS FOUNDATION WILL SUPPORT THE PROJECT BY CONTRIBUTING EXPERTISE IN THE RECRUITMENT OF UNDERSERVED STUDENTS WITHIN COMMUNITIES OF COLOR. PROJECT SOAR WILL EXPAND LUS OUTREACH INTO CHICAGOS ECONOMICALLY DISADVANTAGED GEOGRAPHIC AREAS AND PROVIDE IMMERSIVE AVIATION MAINTENANCE EXPERIENCES FOR HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS, STRENGTHEN EXISTING DUAL CREDIT PROGRAMS, PROVIDE BILINGUAL PROGRAM INFORMATION AND OUTREACH TO HISPANIC STUDENTS AND FAMILIES, AND LAUNCH CAREER EXPOSURE OPPORTUNITIES. LU WILL ALSO RECRUIT AND ENROLL TWO, 18-PERSON COHORTS OF DIVERSE SCHOLARS TO LU TO EARN A P CERTIFICATION AND POTENTIALLY CONTINUE THEIR EDUCATION IN PURSUIT OF ASSOCIATES OR BACHELORS DEGREES IN AVIATION MAINTENANCE PROGRAMS. TO REMOVE FINANCIAL BARRIERS FOR LOW-INCOME STUDENTS, LU WILL PROVIDE SOAR SCHOLARS WITH SCHOLARSHIPS OF $13,000 IN THEIR FIRST YEAR AS WELL AS STIPENDS TO COVER THE COSTS OF PURCHASING THEIR TOOLS AND LATER, SITTING FOR THEIR CERTIFICATION EXAMS. TO PROVIDE ACADEMIC AND SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL SUPPORT, LU WILL ENSURE SOAR SCHOLARS RECEIVE MONTHLY ONE-ON-ONE MENTORING WITH FACULTY, PEER-LED STUDY GROUPS TO PREPARE FOR CERTIFICATION EXAMS, AND CAREER DEVELOPMENT AND PROFESSIONALIZATION (E.G., INDUSTRY SITE VISITS, MOCK INTERVIEWS). LUS INDUSTRY ADVISORY BOARD (IAB) AND A NEWLY DEVELOPED PROJECT SOAR ADVISORY GROUP WILL FACILITATE CAREER DEVELOPMENT FOR BOTH DUAL CREDIT STUDENTS AND SOAR SCHOLARS. FOLLOWING ARE THE PROJECTS OBJECTIVES: (OBJECTIVE 1) EXPAND AND STRENGTHEN PRE-COLLEGE OUTREACH, IMMERSION, AND DUAL CREDIT PARTICIPATION WITH AT LEAST 432 DIVERSE HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS (216 ANNUALLY) AND 100 DUAL CREDIT STUDENTS (50 ANNUALLY) IN PARTNERSHIP WITH SAC, CPASS, SCHOOL DISTRICT 214, AND WILCO. (OBJECTIVE 2) ESTABLISH A SUPPORTIVE COHORT-BASED SCHOLARS PROGRAM FOR 36 FAA SCHOLARS (18 ANNUALLY) AND PROVIDE MENTORING AND ACADEMIC SUPPORT TO ATTAIN A P CERTIFICATIONS AND CONTINUED EDUCATION, AS APPLICABLE. PERFORMANCE MEASURES FOR OBJ. 2 INCLUDE RETAINING AT LEAST 89% OF SCHOLARS ANNUALLY AND CERTIFYING AT LEAST 83% OF SCHOLARS. AS A RESULT, LU ANTICIPATES INCREASING AVIATION MAINTENANCE PROGRAM DIVERSITY BY 5-10% POINTS. (OBJECTIVE 3) WITH INDUSTRY INPUT, EXPAND STUDENTS  CAREER DEVELOPMENT AND PROFESSIONALIZATION OPPORTUNITIES TO BETTER MEET WORKFORCE NEEDS. PERFORMANCE MEASURES INCLUDE INCREASING THE NUMBER OF AVIATION MAINTENANCE STUDENTS PARTICIPATING IN CAREER DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITIES COMPARED TO BASELINE AND ENGAGING IN COMMUNITY-BASED STRATEGIC PLANNING AND ADVISEMENT WITH IAB AND A NEWLY DEVELOPED ADVISORY GROUP ON A QUARTERLY BASIS.

IOWA LAKES IS THE ONLY TWO-YEAR, DEGREE-GRANTING INSTITUTION OF HIGHER EDUCATION IN A 2,900 SQUARE MILE AREA OF RURAL, NORTHWEST IOWA. THE EXISTING AVIATION PROGRAM SERVES A LARGE PERCENTAGE OF THE STATE OF IOWA AND SURROUNDING STATES. THE PROPOSED PROJECT AIMS TO DEVELOP A HIGH SCHOOL AVIATION PROGRAM, EXPAND THE GROWING DRONE PROGRAM, AND DEVELOP A ROTARY WING PROGRAM.THE IOWA LAKES MISSION IS, TO PROVIDE OPPORTUNITIES FOR QUALITY LIFELONG LEARNING AND PROMOTE ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT FOR OUR COMMUNITIES. THE AVIATION PROGRAM HAS REPRESENTATIVES WORKING TOGETHER TO ENSURE NORTHWEST IOWA HAS A SKILLED WORKFORCE, SEEKING OUT NEW STANDARDS-BASED ACTIVITIES, CURRICULUM, MATERIALS, AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT IN ROBOTICS, CODING, AND DRONES, AND IDENTIFYING INDUSTRY PARTNERSHIPS FOR STUDENTS IN STEM FIELDS.IOWA LAKES IS DEVELOPING PROGRAMS THAT SPECIFICALLY RELATE TO THE GROWTH OF THE AVIATION WORKFORCE. THE EXISTING AVIATION AND AIRPORT MANAGEMENT PROGRAM HAS GROWN SUBSTANTIALLY IN RECENT YEARS, INCLUDING BECOMING ONE OF ONLY 23 COLLEGES IN THE COUNTRY TO HOST JUNIOR RESERVE OFFICERS TRAINING CORPS (JROTC) TRAINING UNDER CONTRACT WITH THE U.S. AIR FORCE. HAVING A SOLID FOUNDATION, THE COLLEGE HOPES TO EXPAND OUR CAPABILITY TO FORM A PIPELINE FROM AREA HIGH SCHOOLS. THE INAUGURAL COHORT, AS DESCRIBED IN THE NARRATIVE, WOULD SERVE 50 STUDENTS FROM HIGH SCHOOLS IN ALL FIVE COUNTIES OF THE IOWA LAKES REGION.

negativeFlows.title: THE LOUISIANA ASPIRE - AERIAL SYSTEMS PILOT INSTRUCTION   RESOURCE ENDEAVOR - PROGRAM WILL INCREASE THE SIZE AND QUALITY OF THE AVIATION WORKFORCE BY ADDRESSING BOTH GOALS OF THE FAA AIRCRAFT PILOTS WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT PROGRAM. USING A TRAINING CURRICULUM DEVELOPED BY NATIONALLY RECOGNIZED EDUCATORS TO TRAIN A DIVERSE GROUP OF HIGH SCHOOL EDUCATORS AS SMALL UNMANNED AERIAL SYSTEMS (SUAS) PILOTS AND PROVIDING THE RESOURCES AND GUIDANCE TO ESTABLISH THEIR OWN LOCAL TRAINING PROGRAMS, THIS TRAIN-THE-TRAINER MODEL WILL DEVELOP A NETWORK OF SUAS EDUCATION EFFORTS THAT SERVE A BROAD POPULATION OF LOUISIANA HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS AND GUIDE THEIR GROWTH INTO CERTIFIED SUAS PILOTS. STRATEGIC PARTICIPANT RECRUITMENT EFFORTS WILL ENSURE ENGAGEMENT WITH PUBLIC AND PRIVATE HIGH SCHOOLS IN RURAL, SUBURBAN, AND URBAN AREAS IN THE STATE. IN ADDITION TO TRAINING AT LEAST 40 EDUCATORS AND 800 HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS OVER TWO YEARS, THE ASPIRE PROGRAM ALSO INCORPORATES CASE STUDIES AND MISSION PLANNING WORKFLOWS THAT HIGHLIGHT THE APPLICATIONS OF SUAS AS TOOLS THAT ADDRESS CHALLENGES RELEVANT TO STUDENTS  CAREERS AFTER GRADUATION - TOPICS LIKE COASTAL ENGINEERING, ECOLOGICAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, AND AGRICULTURAL AND INDUSTRIAL ASSET MONITORING. WHETHER ASPIRE GRADUATES ENTER THE WORKFORCE AFTER HIGH SCHOOL OR CONTINUE INTO HIGHER EDUCATION, THE PROGRAM ASSISTS THEM IN IDENTIFYING A CAREER PATH THAT THEY ARE PASSIONATE ABOUT AND SUPPORTING THE PURSUIT OF THEIR GOALS.THE ASPIRE PROGRAM TEAM IS LEAD BY INSTRUCTIONAL FACULTY FROM LOUISIANA STATE UNIVERSITY S DEPARTMENT OF MECHANICAL ENGINEERING AND DEPARTMENT OF OCEANOGRAPHY AND COASTAL SCIENCES, AND SUPPORTED BY WALKER HIGH SCHOOL S DRONE ACADEMY, AND ADVANCED AERIAL EDUCATION. EACH CONTRIBUTES THEIR EXPERTISE, EXPERIENCE, AND PASSION FOR DEVELOPING THE NEXT GENERATION OF WELL-TRAINED, PROFESSIONALLY LICENSED SUAS OPERATORS AND PROVIDING CAREER PATHWAYS TO MEET THE GROWING NEEDS OF THE AVIATION INDUSTRY AND RELATED ECONOMIC ACTIVITIES. THROUGH ITS COMPREHENSIVE PLAN OF PARTNERSHIPS, OUTREACH INITIATIVES, MONITORING MECHANISMS, AND COLLABORATION WITH DIVERSE STAKEHOLDERS, THE ASPIRE PROGRAM CONTRIBUTES TO A MORE EQUITABLE AND SKILLED WORKFORCE WHILE STIMULATING LOCAL ECONOMIC GROWTH AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP.LOUISIANA STATE UNIVERSITY IS AN ACCREDITED INSTITUTE OF HIGHER EDUCATION AND IS APPLYING UNDER THIS ELIGIBLE APPLICANT CATEGORY.THE ASPIRE PROGRAM ADDRESSES THE ELIGIBLE PROJECT CATEGORIES OF PROVIDING PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT TO HIGH SCHOOL EDUCATORS AND DELIVERING CURRICULUM TO PREPARE HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS TO BECOME UNMANNED AIRCRAFT SYSTEM OPERATORS.

ABSTRACT.IN THIS PROPOSAL, GEORGETOWN HIGH SCHOOLA PUBLIC HIGH SCHOOL WITHIN TEXAS EDUCATION AGENCY ACCREDITED GEORGETOWN INDEPENDENT SCHOOL DISTRICT (GISD)PROPOSES BLUE SKIES AHEAD, A PROJECT THAT WILL EXPAND AND ENHANCE UNMANNED AERIAL SYSTEMS (UAS) AND UNMANNED AERIAL VEHICLES (UAV) CURRICULUM AND COURSEWORK FOR HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS AND PROVIDE PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT FOR HIGH SCHOOL EDUCATORS. THROUGH THE REDESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION OF EXISTING COURSES AND CURRICULUM FOR HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS  THE CREATION AND IMPLEMENTATION OF EDUCATOR PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMS  THE DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF COMMUNITY-FACING OUTREACH PROGRAMS FOR A DIVERSE RANGE OF STUDENTS  AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF AVIATION CAREER CURRICULA AND PROGRAMS, BLUE SKIES AHEAD WILL REACH HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS WITH COURSES IN UNMANNED AERIAL SYSTEMS AND VEHICLES, HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS WITH OUTREACH AND CAREER EXPLORATION PROGRAMS, AND EDUCATORS WITH PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT. OUTPUTS WILL INCLUDE AN INCREASE IN THE NUMBER OF STUDENTS THAT GAIN LICENSES AND CERTIFICATIONS IN AVIATION, AN INCREASE IN THE NUMBER OF STUDENTS THAT SEEK TO PURSUE CAREERS IN AVIATION, AND AN INCREASE IN THE NUMBER OF EDUCATORS WHO ARE ALSO TRAINED TO MAKE AN IMPACT ON STUDENTS IN REGIONAL HIGH SCHOOLS. THE KENTON COUNTY AIRPORT BOARD OWNS AND OPERATES THE CINCINNATI NORTHERN KENTUCKY INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT (CVG). CVG IS A MEDIUM HUB COMMERCIAL SERVICE AIRPORT SERVING THE NORTHERN KENTUCKY   GREATER CINCINNATI AREA. CVG CURRENTLY ENGAGES IN WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT IN SEVERAL WAYS.  AS THIS ENGAGEMENT HAS GROWN, CVG STAFF HAS PROVIDED OUTREACH AND PROGRAMMING TO LOCAL YOUTH, AS A STEPPING STONE TO FUTURE CAREER CHOICES.  THESE PROGRAMS, WHILE SUCCESSFUL, HAVE BEEN DECENTRALIZED.  THIS PROPOSAL INTENDS TO FORMALIZE A STRATEGIC WORKFORCE OUTREACH AND ENGAGEMENT PROGRAM, THROUGH HIRING OF DEDICATED STAFF MEMBER(S), TO CONTINUE TO DEVELOP CURRICULUM, ATTEND AND PRODUCE EVENTS, AND DEVELOP AND ENGAGE IN FORMALIZED OUTREACH PROGRAMS FOR YOUTH.  THE PROGRAM GOAL IS TO INCREASE THE AMOUNT OF EXPOSURE TO AVIATION JOBS, SPECIFICALLY AVIATION MECHANICS, THROUGHOUT THE REGION, AND HAVE A POSITIVE IMPACT ON THE WORKFORCE PIPELINE IN THESE INDUSTRIES.  THIS PROGRAM WILL PUT TO USE CVGS EXISTING STRATEGIC WORKFORCE COLLABORATIVE AND WILL INCLUDE REGULAR OUTREACH TO LOCAL SCHOOLS TARGETING HISTORICALLY DISADVANTAGED POPULATIONS.  THE DEDICATED STAFF MEMBERS WILL DEVELOP THE ANNUAL EDUCATION SUMMIT AND THE GUIDE TO INDUSTRY TO INCREASE EDUCATOR AWARENESS FOR HIGH SCHOOLS, AND FURTHER DEVELOP COMMUNITY OUTREACH AND EXPANSION OF THE EXISTING CURRICULUM FOR ELEMENTARY THROUGH HIGH SCHOOL.  THE PROGRAM WILL ALSO INCLUDE THE EXPANSION OF  AVIATION CAMP .

JOHNSON TECHNICAL INSTITUTE (DBA JOHNSON COLLEGE), LOCATED IN SCRANTON, PENNSYLVANIA, SEEKS FEDERAL AVIATION ADMINISTRATION (FAA) WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT GRANT SUPPORT TO ENHANCE AND FURTHER IMPLEMENT A NEW FAA-CERTIFICATED AVIATION TECHNOLOGY ASSOCIATE DEGREE PROGRAM THAT SUCCESSFULLY RECRUITS AND TRAINS STUDENTS TO FILL GROWING, ESSENTIAL REGIONAL AND NATIONAL HIGH TECHNOLOGY WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT NEEDS IN THE AVIATION INDUSTRY. THE ELIGIBLE PROJECT COMPONENTS PROPOSED HEREIN REQUEST FUNDS TO PURCHASE EQUIPMENT IMPROVING A NEW AVIATION TECHNOLOGY ASSOCIATE DEGREE PROGRAM, SUPPORT SCHOLARSHIPS FOR INDIVIDUALS PURSUING EMPLOYMENT IN THE AVIATION MAINTENANCE FIELD, AND PROPOSES OUTREACH  PIPELINE PROGRAMS TO ENCOURAGE SECONDARY SCHOOL STUDENTS TO PURSUE CAREERS IN AVIATION TECHNOLOGY. PROJECT GOALS INCLUDE THE FURTHER DEVELOPMENT OF A WORKING AIRPORT-BASED TRAINING LABORATORY, PIPELINE RECRUITMENT ACTIVITIES FOR MIDDLE AND HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS TO STIMULATE INTEREST IN AVIATION MAINTENANCE TECHNOLOGY CAREERS, AND STUDENT SCHOLARSHIPS TO ASSIST STUDENTS WITH FINANCIAL AID. THE PROJECT WILL DIRECTLY AND FULLY ADDRESS THE GRANT PROGRAMS GOAL TO SUPPORT THE EDUCATION AND RECRUITMENT OF AVIATION MAINTENANCE TECHNICAL WORKERS AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE AVIATION MAINTENANCE WORKFORCE. THE CURRICULUM AND HANDS-ON TRAINING SUPPORTED WILL PROVIDE THE KNOWLEDGE AND EXPERIENCE NECESSARY FOR STUDENTS COMPLETING THE PROGRAM TO SATISFACTORILY COMPLETE THE WRITTEN, ORAL, AND PRACTICAL TESTS REQUIRED TO BE A CERTIFIED AIRFRAME POWERPLANT MECHANIC.

DEVELOP IS A PROGRAM DESIGNED TO TRAIN HIGH SCHOOL TEACHERS AND EQUIP THEM TO TRAIN HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS IN INTRODUCTORY PRINCIPLES TO MANNED AND UNMANNED AIRCRAFT FLIGHT USING IN PERSON, VIRTUAL REALITY, AND ONLINE MEDIA.  THESE THREE MEDIA WILL BE DESIGNED TO CAPTURE, TRAIN, AND DEVELOP TEACHERS THAT WILL NURTURE STUDENT INTEREST IN AVIATION CAREERS BY TEACHING THE NEXT GENERATION OF AIRCRAFT PILOTS AND UAS OPERATORS FROM DIFFERING SOCIO-ECONOMIC BACKGROUNDS, AND ESPECIALLY FOCUSED ON UNDERREPRESENTED AND UNDERSERVED POPULATIONS.
